about.title: Wheatland Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Wheatland is a small community, but its roads carry a steady flow of traffic, and public records show 17 injury collisions and 29 people hurt in the most recent year counted. Rt 65 and SR-65 handle a lot of that traffic, along with Spenceville Road and Wheatland Road, and Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. see more reported crashes than other times of the week. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, sorting out medical care, missed work, and an insurance adjuster's phone calls can feel like a full-time job on top of recovering. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects injured Wheatland residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of the crash, explain your options, and handle communication with insurers so you can focus on healing. There's no cost to connect, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a county road department — may be responsible. An attorney can help identify who's involved before that shorter deadline passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Affect Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault for the crash, but your compensation can be reduced by your share of responsibility. How fault gets assigned early on matters, which is why speaking with an attorney before giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer is worth considering.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in car accident cases, and attorneys in the network work on contingency — meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. That structure lets you get legal help evaluated without any upfront cost.

items.question: I was in a crash on Spenceville Road and the other driver's insurance company already called me. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Anything you say can be used to shift blame or minimize your claim. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on what to say and when.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Wheatland?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government road or entity contributed to the crash, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth getting evidence preserved and a claim assessed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is free, and there's no obligation to move forward after that conversation. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only collect a fee if you recover compensation.
